title: Can You Wag Your Fingers Like WIPERS? 🌧️
description:
Wag your fingers like wipers. Same way... now FASTER! Flipped into a mirror? Your hands are clingy twins. Wiper style makes one finger swing IN while the other swings OUT, and your brain has to referee that. Go faster and the ref gives up, so the twins copy each other. It even happens to two people swinging their legs side by side. Now try to flip it back.
Did yours flip? Yes or no?

The science: in 1984 Scott Kelso asked people to wag both index fingers side to side in the 'wiper' pattern and to speed up. At a critical speed the fingers switched by themselves into the mirror pattern (both moving in and out together), and they did not switch back. Mirror moves are the more stable pattern; keeping the hands on opposite jobs takes more control, and it is the pattern that breaks first at speed (Kelso, American Journal of Physiology, 1984; Haken, Kelso & Bunz, 1985). The same flip shows up between two people who swing their lower legs while watching each other (Schmidt, Carello & Turvey, 1990). WHY the mirror wins is still argued: one camp says your matching muscles, a 2001 Nature study says it is how the move LOOKS to you (Mechsner et al., 2001).
